newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish shares end at record high in upbeat tone.
newsitem.headline: Swedish shares end at record high in upbeat tone.

text.p: Swedish shares ended at a record high on Wednesday, supported by a higher Wall Street close a day earlier and a stronger dollar cheering the market throughout the day.
The exchange's general index rose 1.06 percent 2,508.37 in turnover of 4.98 billion crowns.
Automotive group Volvo was one of the most traded shares. It rose 4.5 to 179.5 partly on earnings from U.S. Chrysler.
Drugs company Astra rose 4.5 crowns to 328.5 on recurring rumours that it will merge with or be taken over by Swiss company Roche.

Investment company Investor, which owns aircraft maker Saab AB, rallied after a trade deal in which Sweden pledged to buy goods from Hungary if Hungary acquires the fighter plane JAS Gripen, which is partly made by Saab. The share climbed nine crowns to 326.

Forestry shares underperformed the general index, despite the strong dollar, after indications about falling product prices. MoDo rose one crown to 202, Stora slipped 0.5 to 92 and SCA ended unchanged at 144 crowns.
